sourcedFrom: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document (ABSENT — no publication year is printed in the document)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Stag Arms's .308 operators manual, which covers its .308 rifles as a family and does not name the Stag 10, so check your rifle against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The book's field strip is short: the rear takedown pin comes out to its stop, the lower pivots away from the upper, and the charging handle and bolt carrier come out the back. Stag Arms tells you not to take the rifle apart any further than its book shows, and the book stops at the bolt, the buffer and spring, and the handguard.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE
steps.action: This guide follows Stag Arms's .308 operators manual, which does not name the Stag 10, so check your rifle against it. Point the muzzle somewhere safe, keep your finger off the trigger, and put the safety selector lever on SAFE before anything else.
steps.aside: Always point the firearm in a safe direction.
steps.quote: Place the safety selector lever (A) on SAFE.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Unloading, page 23

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine release button and pull the magazine down and out. A round can still be in the chamber with the magazine gone, so the next two steps are not optional.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button (B) and pull the magazine (C) down to remove.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Unloading, page 23

steps.title: Bolt locked open
steps.action: Unlock the charging handle and pull it all the way back, then press in the lower part of the bolt catch and let the charging handle go. The bolt stays locked open and any chambered round is thrown clear.
steps.aside: This locks the bolt in the open position.
steps.quote: Unlock and pull the charging handle (D) all the way out and press in on the lower portion of the bolt catch (E).
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Unloading, page 24

steps.title: Chamber looked into
steps.action: Look into the receiver yourself and confirm there is no cartridge in the chamber. Stag Arms asks for this check before cleaning, and before you hand the rifle to anyone.
steps.aside: Verify that the firearm is not loaded before any disassembly or cleaning is begun.
steps.quote: Look into the receiver and verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber (F).
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Unloading, page 25

steps.title: Bolt forward
steps.action: With the rifle proven empty, press the upper part of the bolt catch and let the bolt go forward. Stag Arms starts the takedown with the bolt in the forward position.
steps.aside: Do not disassemble the firearm any further than instructed in this manual.
steps.quote: Verify that bolt is in the forward position.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 26

steps.title: Takedown pin pushed from the left
steps.action: Push in on the rear takedown pin from the left side of the rifle.
steps.quote: Push in on the takedown pin (A) from the left side of the firearm.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 27

steps.title: Takedown pin out to its stop
steps.action: Pull the takedown pin out from the right as far as it will go. It is captive and stays in the rifle — do not try to pull it free.
steps.quote: Pull the takedown pin (A) out as far as it will go. The pin will not be removed from the firearm.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 27

steps.title: Lower pivoted away from the upper
steps.action: Swing the lower receiver down and away from the upper on the front pivot pin. If you want the two halves fully apart, pull the pivot pin out too.
steps.aside: The upper and lower receivers may be separated by pulling out pivot pin (B).
steps.quote: Pivot the lower receiver away from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 28

steps.title: Charging handle and bolt carrier out the back
steps.action: Pull back on the charging handle; it brings the bolt carrier assembly with it, and both come out of the rear of the upper receiver.
steps.quote: Pull back on the charging handle (C) to remove charging handle and bolt carrier assembly (D).
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper receiver, lower receiver, charging handle and bolt carrier assembly: that is the field strip. Stag Arms has the charging handle and carrier cleaned and lubricated at this point; the bolt strip, the buffer and action spring, and the handguard are in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: Clean charging handle and bolt carrier components with a quality gun cleaning solution.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 29

steps.title: Bore patched with solvent
steps.action: Run a cotton patch on a cleaning rod, wetted with cleaning solution, through the bore. Keep going with clean patches until one comes out clean. Do not let the rod scratch the inside of the barrel.
steps.aside: Do not allow cleaning rods to scratch the inside of the barrel or chamber.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel with a cotton patch attached to a cleaning rod.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Barrel, page 39

steps.title: Bronze brush to loosen fouling
steps.action: Put solvent on a bronze bore brush and work it through the barrel to loosen what the patches leave behind.
steps.aside: Repeat with clean patches until patch stays clean.
steps.quote: Apply cleaning solvent to a bronze bore brush to help loosen particles inside the barrel.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Barrel, page 39

steps.title: Dry patch, then a lightly oiled one
steps.action: Finish the bore with a dry patch, then a lightly oiled patch.
steps.quote: run a dry patch through the barrel and then follow with a lightly oiled patch.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Barrel, page 40

steps.title: Chamber scrubbed with a chamber brush
steps.action: Scrub the chamber with solvent on a chamber brush, moving it through several times, then wipe it out with clean patches until one stays clean.
steps.aside: Move the brush through the chamber several times to scrub the inside of the chamber.
steps.quote: Clean the chamber with solvent and a chamber cleaning brush.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Chamber, page 40

steps.title: Chamber dried — not oiled
steps.action: Finish with a dry patch through the chamber and leave it dry. Unlike the bore, the chamber gets no oil.
steps.quote: After cleaning, run a dry patch through the chamber. Do not oil the chamber.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Chamber, page 40

steps.title: Charging handle and carrier cleaned and lubricated
steps.action: Clean the charging handle and the bolt carrier parts with a gun cleaning solution, then lubricate them with a gun lubricant.
steps.aside: Clean charging handle and bolt carrier components with a quality gun cleaning solution.
steps.quote: Lubricate components with a quality gun lubricant.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassembly For Cleaning — Remove Bolt Carrier, page 29

steps.title: Metal wiped, then lightly oiled
steps.action: Wipe every metal surface with a clean cloth, then go over it again with a lightly oiled cloth.
steps.aside: Use a cleaning solution that is designed for use on firearms.
steps.quote: Wipe all metal surfaces with a clean cloth and then follow up with a lightly oiled cloth.
steps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Cleaning — Cleaning The Exterior, page 40

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out
deepSteps.action: With the bolt carrier assembly out of the rifle, take out the firing pin retaining pin.
deepSteps.aside: Do not disassemble the firearm any further than instructed in this manual.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin (A).
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 29

deepSteps.title: Bolt pushed to the locked position
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt back into the carrier to its locked position.
deepSteps.quote: Push the bolt assembly (B) into the bolt carrier to the locked position as illustrated in figure 30.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 29

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out the rear
deepSteps.action: Slide the firing pin out through the rear of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin (C) through the rear of the bolt carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 30

deepSteps.title: Cam pin out
deepSteps.action: Take the bolt cam pin out of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Remove bolt cam pin (D) from bolt carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 30

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Draw the bolt out of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Remove bolt assembly (B) from bolt carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 30

deepSteps.title: Extractor tested — removed only if it sticks
deepSteps.action: Push in on the back of the extractor. If it springs back, leave it on the bolt. Only if it does not spring back does it come off for cleaning: push the extractor pin out.
deepSteps.aside: Push extractor pin (F) out to remove extractor.
deepSteps.quote: Push in on the rear (E) of the extractor. If the extractor does not spring back, remove the extractor from the bolt for cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 30

deepSteps.title: Extractor off — insert left in its spring
deepSteps.action: Take the extractor pin and the extractor off the bolt. Leave the insert inside the extractor spring; Stag Arms says not to remove it.
deepSteps.quote: Remove extractor pin (F) and extractor (G) from bolt (B). Do not remove insert (I) from extractor spring (H).
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 31

deepSteps.title: Bolt parts cleaned and lubricated
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt and bolt carrier parts with a gun cleaning solution and lubricate them with a gun lubricant.
deepSteps.aside: Replacement parts must be installed by a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: Clean bolt and bolt carrier components with a quality gun cleaning solution. Lubricate components with a quality gun lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Disassemble Bolt, page 31

deepSteps.title: Buffer released past its retainer
deepSteps.action: Confirm again the rifle is not loaded. Hold the buffer in against its spring and press down on the buffer retainer, then let the buffer come forward under control.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the buffer in and press down on retainer to release buffer.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Remove Buffer And Action Spring, page 34

deepSteps.title: Buffer and action spring out
deepSteps.action: Take out the buffer and the action spring.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Remove Buffer And Action Spring, page 34

deepSteps.title: Buffer and spring cleaned and lubricated
deepSteps.action: Clean the buffer and spring with a gun cleaning solution and lubricate them with a gun lubricant.
deepSteps.aside: Lubricate components with a quality gun lubricant.
deepSteps.quote: Clean buffer and spring components with a quality gun cleaning solution.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Remove Buffer And Action Spring, page 35

deepSteps.title: Handguard screws out
deepSteps.action: Confirm the rifle is not loaded, then take out the two socket head screws that hold the handguard.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Remove Handguard, page 38

deepSteps.title: Handguard slid off — watch the spacers
deepSteps.action: Slide the handguard off the front of the rifle. The spacer on each side is loose and can drop out, so catch them. This is the last strip the book publishes.
deepSteps.aside: Do not disassemble the firearm any further than instructed in this manual.
deepSteps.quote: Slide handguard off end of rifle. Spacers (B) on each side are loose and may fall out when handguard is removed.
deepSteps.cite: .308 Operators Manual — ABSENT — no edition is printed in the document — Remove Handguard, page 38

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Cotton patches wetted with cleaning solution until a patch stays clean
Bronze bore brush with solvent to loosen fouling
A dry patch, then a lightly oiled patch
Do not let the cleaning rod scratch the inside of the barrel

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush and solvent, several passes
Clean patches until one stays clean, then a dry patch

cleaning.name: CHARGING HANDLE & BOLT CARRIER
tasks: Charging handle and bolt carrier parts cleaned with a gun cleaning solution

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: All metal surfaces wiped with a clean cloth
Then wiped with a lightly oiled cloth

reassembly: If the bolt was stripped: stagger the gaps of the three gas rings 120° apart around the bolt — never lined up. Put the extractor, with its insert and spring, back on the bolt and push in the extractor pin; the pin must not stick out of the bolt on either side.

Bolt into the carrier, then the cam pin — the hole in the cam pin lines up with the hole through the bolt. Firing pin in through the rear of the carrier, pull the bolt out, and fit the firing pin retaining pin.
If the buffer was out: action spring onto the buffer and into the receiver; press down on the retainer, push the buffer past it, and let the retainer go.
Charging handle engaged and partly in; bolt carrier in so the slot in the carrier takes the tab on the charging handle; push both home into the upper.
Selector on SAFE, swing the lower back up to the upper, and push the takedown pin in. If the handguard was off: handguard, spacers and both screws back on, and the screws tightened.
